reading.title: The Cane Toad: A Cure Worse Than the Disease
reading.intro_zh: 本文讲述一个真实的“好心办坏事”案例——1935 年澳大利亚引进甘蔗蟾蜍来除虫，结果蟾蜍非但没解决问题，反而成了更大的生态灾难。内容改编自澳大利亚入侵物种委员会（Invasive Species Council）的权威资料。
passage: In 1935, Australian sugar growers faced a stubborn enemy: beetles whose larvae devoured the roots of their cane. Searching for a cheap, natural remedy, officials settled on the cane toad, a heavy amphibian native to the Americas that was said to be a voracious eater of insects. Roughly a hundred toads were imported from Hawaii, bred near Cairns, and their thousands of offspring were released into the fields. Astonishingly, no one had ever confirmed that the toad would actually eat the cane beetle, nor had anyone assessed how it might behave in an unfamiliar landscape.

The experiment was a spectacular failure on its own terms. The beetles, which fed and bred high on the cane stalks, were largely beyond the reach of a ground-dwelling toad, and cane-sugar harvests showed no improvement; the pest is now managed with chemicals instead. Yet the toad itself thrived. Each female can lay up to 35,000 eggs in a single clutch, and the species spread relentlessly across the north. Today cane toads occupy more than 1.3 million square kilometres, and the advancing front of the invasion now pushes forward by fifty to sixty kilometres a year.

The deepest damage is chemical. Glands behind the toad's head secrete a potent toxin, so native predators that have never encountered it—freshwater crocodiles, goannas, snakes and the cat-sized northern quoll—are often poisoned the moment they bite. In some regions more than ninety percent of quolls have vanished. The cane toad has become a textbook lesson in unintended consequences: a solution designed to remove one nuisance instead unleashed a far larger and effectively permanent problem, and authorities now concede that eradicating the toad across the continent is impossible.

questions.question: What is the main point of the passage?
options: Cane toads are an effective and inexpensive way to protect sugar crops.
A solution introduced to fix one problem ended up causing a much worse one.
Australian beetles are now the country's most destructive agricultural pest.
Native Australian predators have learned to eat cane toads safely.
questions.explanation_zh: 全文围绕“引进蟾蜍治虫，却制造了更大灾难”这一主旨：方法没解决旧问题，反而带来新的、更严重的后果，因此选 B。

questions.question: According to the passage, how many eggs can a single female cane toad lay in one clutch?
options: Up to 35,000 eggs.
About 2,400 eggs.
Roughly one hundred eggs.
Around 1.3 million eggs.
questions.explanation_zh: 第二段明确说 Each female can lay up to 35,000 eggs in a single clutch，所以选 A（35,000 eggs）。其他数字在文中指的是别的事物（占地面积、引进数量等）。

questions.question: Why did the toads fail to control the cane beetles?
options: The toads refused to eat any insects at all.
Chemical pesticides killed the toads before they could feed.
The beetles lived high on the cane stalks, out of a ground-dwelling toad's reach.
There were too few toads released to make any difference.
questions.explanation_zh: 第二段解释失败原因：甲虫在蔗秆高处取食繁殖，超出了只能在地面活动的蟾蜍的捕食范围，因此选 C。

questions.question: What can be inferred about how the introduction was planned?
options: It was based on years of careful field testing in Australia.
It was carried out hastily, without verifying the toad's usefulness or its risks.
It was opposed by the sugar growers from the very beginning.
It was designed mainly to study the toad's poison glands.
questions.explanation_zh: 第一段指出“没有人确认蟾蜍会吃甘蔗甲虫，也没人评估它在陌生环境中的行为”，可推断引进过程草率、缺乏验证，故选 B。

questions.question: In the first paragraph, the word "voracious" most nearly means
options: very slow and unwilling to move.
harmless and gentle toward other animals.
rare and difficult to find.
extremely hungry and eating large amounts.
questions.explanation_zh: voracious 形容“食量极大、贪吃的”。文中说蟾蜍被认为是 a voracious eater of insects（吃昆虫极厉害），与第四项 D（extremely hungry and eating large amounts）完全吻合，所以选 D。

writing.intro_zh: 今天把 Lesson 59 的五个循环喜剧句式提升到 B2+ 难度：used to 写过去的旧习惯，Every time...would...until... 写反复发生的动作，spent...training...to... 写训练过程，so that...would... 写目的，As soon as...until... 写循环里的先后步骤。请用更抽象、更复杂的语境来仿写。

patterns.title: used to ...
patterns.source: Rex used to sit outside our front gate and bark.
patterns.focus_zh: used to 用来写过去经常发生、现在已经变化的习惯，是 Lesson 59 开头的旧问题。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写在某项新技术或新制度出现之前，某个人或某个机构过去长期坚持的旧做法。
patterns.sample: Before the smart thermostat arrived, my grandmother used to adjust every radiator in the house by hand each morning.
patterns.tip_zh: used to 后面接动词原形；它强调 old habit，不要写成 is used to。

patterns.title: Every time ..., ... would ... until ...
patterns.source: Every time he wanted to come into the garden he would bark until someone opened the gate.
patterns.focus_zh: 这个句式把“条件一出现 -> 动作反复发生 -> 到某个结果才停止”的循环写清楚。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写每当某个条件出现时，某个团队或系统会反复做某件事，直到某个结果出现才停下来。
patterns.sample: Every time the committee postponed a decision, the engineers would keep redesigning the prototype until someone finally approved a budget.
patterns.tip_zh: Every time 后面写触发条件；until 后面写这个动作停止的时间点。

patterns.title: spent weeks training ... to ...
patterns.source: My husband spent weeks training him to press his paw on the latch.
patterns.focus_zh: spent + time + training + object + to do 可以写“花时间训练某人学会一个动作”。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写某个机构或专家花了相当长的时间训练某些人、动物或模型去掌握一项复杂的技能。
patterns.sample: The conservation team spent three seasons training the rescued falcons to hunt independently before releasing them into the wild.
patterns.tip_zh: spent 后面先接时间；training 后面接被训练的人，再用 to do 写学会的动作。

patterns.title: so that ... would ...
patterns.source: This time he was barking so that someone would let him out.
patterns.focus_zh: so that 后面说明目的：做这个动作，是为了让别人做另一件事。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写某人或某组织有意做某个动作，目的是让另一方注意到、配合或采取某种行动。
patterns.sample: The startup deliberately leaked a few details to journalists so that the wider public would notice its product before the official launch.
patterns.tip_zh: so that 前面写动作；would 后面写别人会做的事，目的关系要清楚。

patterns.title: As soon as ..., ... until ...
patterns.source: As soon as he opens the gate from the outside, he comes into the garden and waits until the gate shuts.
patterns.focus_zh: As soon as 写“刚一发生”，until 写“等到某个时刻为止”，适合描写循环里的步骤。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写一个系统或机制一旦检测到某个信号，就持续做出反应，直到某个指标恢复正常为止。
patterns.sample: As soon as the algorithm detects a sudden spike in traffic, it keeps spinning up new servers until the response time returns to normal.
patterns.tip_zh: As soon as 句首要接一个动作；until 后面接等待结束的信号。
